source.title: Feature Learning in L2-regularized DNNs: Attraction/Repulsion and Sparsity
source.authors: Arthur Jacot; E. Golikov; Clément Hongler; Franck Gabriel

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendix, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports width-sweep training-loss results for L2-regularized networks, conceptually related to training outcomes, but does not measure the classification-error behavior named by the versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own width-sweep results for training loss. It does not state training classification error, so these results do not map to a claim version. Cited results from other work are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes sparsity and attainable L2-regularized loss as width increases. Its experiments measure regularized loss rather than training classification error or the frequency of spurious minima in the specified two-layer teacher-student setting. It does not test initialization, depth degradation, learning-rate stability, or batch normalization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors derive representation and covariance reformulations and prove a width-independent plateau in the optimal L2-regularized loss for sufficiently wide positively homogeneous networks. They establish a worst-case quadratic width requirement and observe much earlier empirical plateaus, while explicitly withholding any guarantee that training reaches global minima.
record.recipe_differences: The empirical experiments use L2-regularized loss and width sweeps, not the random-initialization benchmark classification-error recipes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported width-sweep plateau differs by dataset/loss setting; the teacher-network plot selects the lowest-loss result from three trials, and some trials remain above the plateau.

fits_no_version.finding: Reported regularized training loss plateaus around width 10 in depth-3 fully connected networks on a 1,000-example MNIST subset and synthetic teacher data. The teacher-data curve selects the best of three trials; some other trials remain above the plateau.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In these L2-regularized depth-3 settings, attained training loss can plateau at modest widths, without establishing that all runs reach the global minimum.

fits_no_version.finding: For positively homogeneous networks, the global minimum of the L2-regularized objective is independent of hidden widths once every hidden layer has at least N(N+1) neurons. A constructed dataset requires at least N²/4 neurons to attain the optimum.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Width bounds for attaining the optimal regularized objective characterize representational sparsity, without guaranteeing that gradient training finds that optimum.

record.problems: The authors state they cannot guarantee the procedures approach a global minimum. For the teacher setting, they select the lowest-loss result among three trials; some trials remain above the plateau, and it is unclear whether longer training would help. The reported plots do not provide exact values in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No reported width-sweep result was omitted. Cited prior-work findings were excluded.

untested.parts: Training classification error in convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted labels and the specified training recipes.
Spurious-minimum frequencies under gradient descent in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, including matched widths and one or two extra student neurons.
Depth degradation and its prevention through identity shortcuts, special tanh initialization, or Fixup.
Initialization-dependent training speed, signal and gradient propagation, and trainable depth.
Recovery, divergence, and sharpness dynamics relative to learning-rate stability thresholds.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The discussion of large learning rates cites prior work rather than reporting a stability experiment. Appendix C.1 constructs a shallow ReLU local minimum, but does not analyze the teacher-student setting or width-dependent gradient-descent outcomes named by V2.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, optimizer-specific outcomes, and effects of early stopping or regularization on classification error.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student gradient descent and student width relative to teacher width.
Depth-related training classification error, identity shortcuts, deep plain tanh networks, and residual networks without normalization.
Initialization comparisons, signal or gradient propagation, and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss recovery or divergence, and sharpness during training.
Batch-normalization comparisons of training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

rows.subject: fully-connected DNNs of depth L = 3
rows.operation_detail: Compared train loss across network widths for cross-entropy training with L2 regularization.

conditions.value: L2; two values of λ, not stated

rows.measure: Train loss as a function of width; the authors state the plateau appears to start around 10.
rows.note: The plot reports a width sweep and the text describes a plateau around width 10. It does not report classification error.
rows.check: The width-dependent loss plateau is reported, but it cannot establish any version's effect. The training loss includes the L2 penalty; a plateau does not establish near-zero classification error. Exact loss values and the two regularization strengths cannot be recovered from the supplied figure caption.

rows.subject: fully-connected DNNs of depth L = 3
rows.size_stated: varying widths; synthetic teacher network has widths n = (50, 10, 10, 10)
rows.operation_detail: Compared train loss across network widths for MSE training with L2 regularization.

conditions.value: N = 1000 Gaussian inputs and outputs evaluated on a fixed teacher network
three independent networks per width; lowest-loss network selected

rows.measure: Train loss as a function of width; the authors state the plateau appears to start around 10.
rows.note: The reported curve uses the lowest-loss network among three trials at each width. The authors say some trials remain above the plateau even at large widths and may be stuck or may need longer training. This is a loss result, not classification error.
rows.check: The regularized MSE plateau cannot establish any version's effect. This is a depth-3 teacher-student setting, without the two-layer local-minimum frequency comparison required by V2. The curve selects the lowest final loss among three trials at each width; it does not represent typical success. Above-plateau trials are not established local minima.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
